intended_user: Only physicians with adequate training and experience in bronchoscopic techniques and adequate healthcare facilities should perform procedures with the Ion endoluminal system. Training provided by Intuitive is limited to the use of the Ion endoluminal system and does not replace the necessary medical training and experience required to perform diagnostic and therapeutic bronchoscopy procedures.

warnings.text: Alerts the reader about a situation which, if not avoided, could result in death or serious injury. 1.4 Professional Instructions for Use Essential Prescribing Information • Device Name: Intuitive Ion Endoluminal System and Instruments (IF1000). • Rx only: Federal Law (USA) restricts this device to sale by or on the order of a physician (or properly licensed practitioner). Indications for Use The Ion endoluminal system (Model IF1000), referred to in this manual as “the system,” assists the user in navigating a catheter and endoscopic tools in the pulmonary tract using endoscopic visualization of the tracheobronchial tree for diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. The Ion endoluminal system enables fiducial marker placement. It does not make a diagnosis and is not for pediatric use. The PlanPoint Software uses patient CT scans to create a 3D plan of the lung and navigation pathways for use with the Ion endoluminal system. The Flexision Biopsy Needle is used with the Ion endoluminal system to biopsy tissue from a target area in the lung. Introduction | Professional Instructions for Use 11

warnings.text: To avoid patient injury, always lock the wheels of the System Cart before docking to the patient. • Ensure the System Cart power cable can reach a power outlet. • Ensure the System Cart is adjacent to the procedure table (bed), with the Power button facing the bed. • Ensure there is enough room for the fluoroscope to move around the bed. • Ensure the System Cart is at or near the head of the bed. • Ensure the physician can easily view the monitors. • Ensure the System Cart does not interfere with other equipment in the room. • Ensure there are no obstructions around the arm. • Once positioned, apply the foot brake and un-stow the monitors. • Ensure the bed brakes are locked before starting the procedure. Move and Position the Controller Guidelines to Move the Controller • Release the brakes on the wheels. • Tilt the Controller and push to transport the Controller. Guidelines to Position the Controller in the Procedure Room • Ensure the physician can view the monitors and reach the arm. • Ensure the Controller cable can reach the connector on the System Cart. • Ensure there is space to move the Controller out of the way during biopsy, if needed. 48 Room Setup

notes.text: If Controller responsiveness is poor, change or dry gloves. The Controller touchscreen and scroll wheel are designed to sense touch. Wet gloves may interfere with touch sensing. Figure 4.19 Controller 5 10 9 3 2 4 1 7 6 8 The Controller has the following components: 1. Handle: Provides grasp for transport of the Controller. 2. Emergency stop (E-stop) button: Stops system operation at any time and causes the Catheter tip to go inactive. 3. Scroll wheel: Controls the insertion and retraction of the Catheter. Roll it towards the touchscreen to insert the Catheter, and roll it away from the touchscreen to retract it. 4. Passive button: Controls the Catheter state (active and passive). Quick-press this button to relax the Catheter tip (passive), and press it again to resume active mode. Press and hold to slowly relax the Catheter tip (temporary passive). Release the button to stop relaxing the Catheter and resume active mode. 5. Touchscreen: Controls to select targets, save images and videos, and provide other options described in this manual. notes.text: the various preview modes and options: • Lock to Path mode: On by default, Lock to Path locks the Navi- gation View to the path towards the selected destination. Lock to Path mode forces the Navigation View to remain on the path to the target, but still follows the insertion motion of the real Catheter, and can be used with the Live View to accurately facil- itate navigation to the target. While relying on the Live View, use Lock to Path to indicate which turns to make. If there is divergence between the Live View and Navigation View, use the arrows that appear on the touchscreen to adjust the insertion or retraction of the Navigation View to match the Live View. Use the Move Target or Catheter reference function- ality to help localize the target. • Preview Path mode: Tap Scroll Wheel Lock to unlock Lock to Path and enter Preview Path to preview the selected path to the target without moving the actual Catheter. Use the arrows to move the Navigation View Catheter forward or backward through the airway. See Figure 4.22. • Vasculature: Depicts both arteries and veins in red. Tap Vascu- lature to toggle the visibility of any vasculature that was added during planning. Vasculature is visible only in the Navigation View when either Preview Path or Lock to Path mode is active. Adjust Tree Tap and hold with one finger to rotate, tap and hold with two fingers to pan, and pinch to zoom into the airway tree on the monitor. The Tree View is set to follow Catheter movement by default and stops when the tree is rotated. Recenter to follow the Catheter movement again. The Tree View can be rotated only in manual view. You can also toggle the visibility of the target, reference areas, and anatomy borders. • Airway Tree: Tap Airway Tree to view the approximate shape of the Catheter within the airways. If the target is updated, the option to switch to Airway Tree is disabled until the target is reset. • Set the angle for Tree View to match the fluoroscope angle, or input any desired angle by tapping Adjust Angle on the Con- troller touchscreen. Rotate the Tree View to get the optimal angle for viewing by tapping the view orientations on the Con- troller touchscreen (Axial, Sagittal, Coronal, Follow, Manual, and Adjust Angle). Tap Coronal to rotate the tree to the anterior- posterior view. (continues on next page) 44 System Overview | Controller Use

notes.text: Before clinical use, always inspect the system and Controller for any damage (for example, broken, cracked, chipped, or worn parts). If you observe any damage, contact Customer Service and do not use the system. 1. Power on the system by pressing the Power button on the System Cart. The system must be plugged in to begin a procedure. If the System Cart is powered on before the Controller cable is attached, attach the cable to the System Cart and then restart the system. 2. Unfold the monitors. Position the screens for optimal viewing. 3. Connect the fluoroscope and other auxiliary devices to the system (for example, standard bronchoscope, R-EBUS) and power them on: • Connect the devices to the System Cart using the appropriate cables. • Confirm the connections are secure. • Power on the fluoroscope and other auxiliary devices. Once a connection is established, the label of the connection illuminates blue on the auxiliary connection panel. For further information, see 6.3 Auxiliary Connections on page 52. 4. Remove the trackball and scroll wheel, clean them with saline and dry with gauze. Reinstall the trackball and scroll wheel into the Controller and wait for calibration to complete. 5. Follow Guided Setup instructions on the top monitor.
